name: peer_escalation
description: Wraps core/peer_cli.py's read-only discovery/selection/preview logic (which peer CLIs — Claude Code, Qwen CLI, Gemini CLI — are installed, task-type classification, CLI selection, prompt preview) as CCOS capabilities. Deliberately does NOT expose escalate(), confirm(), or call() from core/peer_cli.py, nor run_peer/run_direct/run_prompted/run_positional from core/peer_shell.py — those spawn real subprocess/pexpect sessions with external CLIs and, per CODEY_OS_MASTER_VISION.md, require the existing interactive terminal consent prompt (PeerCLIManager.confirm()) before any file contents leave the device. That consent step has no meaning behind an automated capability call, so wrapping it would either hang on stdin or bypass consent outright. Same risk class as daemon_control's unwrapped 'command' handler and finetune's unwrapped model-swap functions, left unwrapped pending Ish's explicit decision. Existing callers verified 2026-07-30: the actual escalate() call site is core/agent.py:1781 (not :1715 as this description previously and incorrectly said); main.py has no escalate() call at all — main.py:1019's '/peer' handler only lists/inspects available peer CLIs via get_peer_cli_manager(), it never calls escalate(). Both untouched and remain the only real path to escalation; this manifest's line-number citations were stale and are corrected here per the tool/capability audit.

capabilities.name: coding.peer_list_available
capabilities.description: Read-only: list peer CLIs (claude/gemini/qwen) detected as installed on this device

capabilities.name: coding.peer_detect_task_type
capabilities.description: Read-only: classify a message/error log into the task type escalate() would use (debugging/refactor/generate/review/explain/complex/default)

capabilities.name: coding.peer_select_cli
capabilities.description: Read-only: which installed peer CLI would be picked for a given task type, without calling it

capabilities.name: coding.peer_build_prompt
capabilities.description: Read-only: preview the exact prompt text that would be sent to a peer CLI if escalation proceeded, without sending it

author: CCOS
